summary: Ahead of the ICC Men's ODI World Cup 2023 final between India and Australia on November 19 at Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, this article reviews all 13 prior World Cup meetings of the two sides. Australia leads with eight wins, but India has won the last two, most recently in Chennai in 2023. It recalls the painful 2003 final loss to Australia in Johannesburg and asks whether India can win a third title.
one_line: A match-by-match review of India vs Australia's 13 previous ODI World Cup meetings, ahead of the 2023 final in Ahmedabad.
key_facts: The ICC Men's ODI World Cup 2023 final between India and Australia was scheduled for Sunday, November 19 at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad.
India are two-time World Champions and Australia are five-time World Champions; this is India's fourth World Cup final and Australia's eighth.
India and Australia have met 13 times in ODI World Cups before this final, with Australia winning eight; India has won the last two meetings.
In the 2003 final in Johannesburg, India chose to bowl first; Australia scored 360 and Ricky Ponting made 140 off 121 balls, and India were bowled out for 234, with Virender Sehwag making 82 off 81.
In the 2003 league match in Centurion, India collapsed for 125 in 41.4 overs, and Australia won by nine wickets with 166 balls remaining.
The 1987 match in Chennai was decided by a single run in Australia's favour, with Geoff Marsh scoring 110 and India bowled out for 269 in 49.5 overs.
In the 1992 Brisbane match, India lost by one run on a revised target of 236 off 47 overs after rain, with two run-outs on the last ball; Mohammad Azharuddin scored 93.
India beat Australia by five wickets in the 2011 quarter-final in Ahmedabad, chasing 261 in 47.4 overs, and went on to beat Sri Lanka in the final.
Australia beat India by 95 runs in the 2015 semi-final in Sydney after Steven Smith scored 105 off 93 balls, and later won the title against New Zealand.
In 2019 at The Oval, India won by 36 runs after Shikhar Dhawan made 117 off 109 and Virat Kohli 82 off 77 in a total of 353.
In the 2023 Chennai league match, Australia were all out for 199-200 in 49.3 overs; India lost three wickets for two runs but won by six wickets as KL Rahul scored 97 and Virat Kohli 85.
In 1983, Australia beat India by 162 runs in Nottingham, but India won by 118 runs in Chelmsford and went on to win their first World Cup, beating the West Indies in the final.
